newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Commonwealth Bank union members stop work.
newsitem.headline: Commonwealth Bank union members stop work.

text.p: Members of the Finance Sector Union (FSU) employed by Commonweath Bank of Australia (CBA) will hold stop work meetings on Monday to discuss a proposed contract which the union says pares back the rights of bank employees.

"More than 25,000 members will participate in the nation-wide stop work meetings on Monday in response to the CBA's intention to downgrade employees' working conditions," the union said in a statement. "It is likely most CBA branches will be closed between 9 a.m and 10.30 a.m., the duration of the stop work meetings."
The bank has said it expects about half its 1,500 branches to be closed during the meetings. Electronic banking is unaffected.
The union claims the bank is threatening rights to days off, redundancy, sick leave and career options under a proposed new enterprise bargaining agreement.
"Certainly the union's action doesn't help the negotiation process," the bank's corporate relations manager, Lyndell Fraser, told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
Fraser said the bank was committed to its proposals.
"We're about getting fair remuneration for our staff and getting on with keeping them in jobs," Fraser said. "That way we serve customers and make a contribution to the whole economy."
